1→# Yawble core

A harness for agent teams. One Concierge per signed-in person, headless members under it, and a message log that decides who wakes.

The code name is **Harness**; the brand is **Yawble**, and it lives in two presentation files (`web/src/presentation/product.ts` and `productName` in `web/package.json`). The brand does not appear in environment variables, paths, or identifiers, and a test refuses it anywhere else.

## What runs

- **Host** (`src/Harness.Host`) — the HTTP API, the MCP server at `/mcp`, and the built web app.
10→- **Web** (`web/`) — the Quasar board.
- There is **no platform CLI** for agents. Agents call MCP tools. The **operator CLI**, `yawble`, is for the person who runs an instance (install, start, update, diagnose, remote access) and lives in [`cli/`](cli/README.md), released with the image under the same version.

## Container

Podman (or Docker), run by the operator CLI. SQLite and the rest of the instance live on a named volume, so rebuilding the image does not wipe teams.

```powershell
scripts\dev-up.ps1
```
20→
That builds the `yawble` CLI into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\yawble` and an image from this checkout tagged `localhost/yawble:dev-<commit>`, points yawble at it with `yawble config set image`, and runs `yawble up`: the pod and container `yawble`, the volume `yawble-data` mounted at `/data` (`HARNESS_DATA_ROOT`), port 8080. Each build gets its own tag because `yawble up` replaces the container only when a setting changes. Limits and secrets are yawble's own settings, set once: `yawble config set memory 12g`, `cpus 8`, `maxRunning 8`; `yawble github` or `<command> | yawble secret set NAME`.

The published image is `ghcr.io/djlsystems/yawble`, one manifest for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, built and pushed by `scripts\release.ps1` (below) under the release's version tag and `latest`. The operator CLI pins one of those version tags and never pulls `latest`. `scripts\dev-up.ps1` builds a local image for this machine's architecture from the working tree instead; both come from the same `Containerfile`. The arm64 half is built under emulation, which the release script checks for and explains how to register.

**Operator switches.** `dotnet Harness.Host.dll --DataRoot=/data --doctor` prints one JSON line describing the data root, the database and its schema verdict, the backups, and each agent CLI's install and sign-in state, then exits without serving. The data root comes first: ASP.NET's command-line provider would otherwise take it as `--doctor`'s value (inside the container `HARNESS_DATA_ROOT` is set, so the switch alone also works there). It is safe while the host runs; the operator CLI calls it with `podman exec`. The other switches are `--backup [path]`, `--restore <path>`, `--reset-password <email>` and `--list-users`; `--restore` or `--reset-password` given no value prints the list.

**A volume created before the schema squash must be recreated.** The database now has one schema step per store: `auth-001`, `messages-001`, `skill-001` and `backlog-001`. A volume written by an earlier build still records the old step ids, and the host will not start on it. It says the database "was written by a newer build" and lists the old ids. There is no upgrade path. Take off the volume anything you want to keep, because this deletes every team, account and saved agent login on it, then run:

```powershell
30→yawble down
podman rm -f yawble
podman volume rm yawble-data
scripts\dev-up.ps1
```

**Use Podman's default, rootless machine.** The port is published as `0.0.0.0:8080:8080` and that is deliberate: on Windows, WSL relays to `localhost` only the IPv4 ports a process inside the machine is listening on. A rootless machine publishes through pasta, which listens, and the explicit `0.0.0.0` makes it bind IPv4 rather than an IPv6 dual-stack socket. A rootful machine publishes with firewall rules that WSL never sees, so `localhost:8080` stays silent there; `yawble up` offers to make it rootless. The fix is the machine flag, `podman machine set --rootful=false` with the machine stopped, because the connection default alone is put back to rootful on every machine start. Mirrored WSL networking is not an answer: it stops the Podman machine's own services from starting.

The image already contains the toolchain an agent is expected to find: the .NET 10 SDK, Node 22 and npm, Python 3 (pip and venv), uv, Go, git, the GitHub CLI, a C compiler, jq, ripgrep, fd, and sqlite. Package caches for NuGet, Go, npm, and pip live on the data volume. A JDK, Rust, PHP, Ruby, and Docker are not installed.

40→Every start checks the data volume for `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, and `grok`. Anything missing is downloaded there, so the next image rebuild does not fetch them again.

API keys are not downloaded. Give them to yawble (`yawble secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`; `yawble github` for `GH_TOKEN`) and run `yawble up`. yawble keeps them in its own env file, readable only by you, and hands it to the container; nothing is copied into the image. Logins those CLIs save for themselves also persist, because `HOME` is `/data/agent-home` on the same volume.

**Backups.** The host writes a daily `VACUUM INTO` copy of the database to `/data/backups` and keeps the newest seven. That copy lives on the same volume, so also export the whole volume from time to time with `podman volume export`. Both, and how to restore them, are in [docs/ops/backups-logs-and-versions.md](docs/ops/backups-logs-and-versions.md).

**Watching a folder.** A folder-change trigger watches the team's documents with no setup. To watch a network share, mount it on the Windows host, pass it in with another `podman run -v`, and list it under `FileBrowser:Roots` with `"allowWatch": true`. The steps, fields and limits are in [docs/ops/folder-change-triggers.md](docs/ops/folder-change-triggers.md).

`GET /api/agents/auth` reports, per preset, whether the command is on `PATH` and whether it looks authenticated. The board shows a banner when a command is installed but the probe says it is not.

50→**Updating and releasing.** `scripts\update.ps1` pulls `main`, waits until no agent is running in the container, rebuilds with `dev-up.ps1` and prints the version now running. `scripts\release.ps1` runs both suites, tags `v<yyyy.mm.dd.N>`, publishes the GitHub Release and pushes the image to ghcr.io; `-DryRun` stops before publishing. Both are described in [docs/ops/releases-and-updates.md](docs/ops/releases-and-updates.md).

The data root comes first: ASP.NET's command-line provider would otherwise take it as `--doctor`'s value (inside the container `HARNESS_DATA_ROOT` is set, so the switch alone also works there). It is safe while the host runs; the operator CLI calls it with `podman exec`. The other switches are `--backup [path]`, `--restore <path>`, `--reset-password <email>` and `--list-users`; `--restore` or `--reset-password` given no value prints the list.

**A volume created before the schema squash must be recreated.** The database now has one schema step per store: `auth-001`, `messages-001`, `skill-001` and `backlog-001`. A volume written by an earlier build still records the old step ids, and the host will not start on it. It says the database "was written by a newer build" and lists the old ids. There is no upgrade path. Take off the volume anything you want to keep, because this deletes every team, account and saved agent login on it, then run:

```powershell
yawble down
podman rm -f yawble
podman volume rm yawble-data
scripts\dev-up.ps1
```

**Use Podman's default, rootless machine.** The port is published as `0.0.0.0:8080:8080` and that is deliberate: on Windows, WSL relays to `localhost` only the IPv4 ports a process inside the machine is listening on. A rootless machine publishes through pasta, which listens, and the explicit `0.0.0.0` makes it bind IPv4 rather than an IPv6 dual-stack socket. A rootful machine publishes with firewall rules that WSL never sees, so `localhost:8080` stays silent there; `yawble up` offers to make it rootless. The fix is the machine flag, `podman machine set --rootful=false` with the machine stopped, because the connection default alone is put back to rootful on every machine start. Mirrored WSL networking is not an answer: it stops the Podman machine's own services from starting.

The image already contains the toolchain an agent is expected to find: the .NET 10 SDK, Node 22 and npm, Python 3 (pip and venv), uv, Go, git, the GitHub CLI, a C compiler, jq, ripgrep, fd, and sqlite. Package caches for NuGet, Go, npm, and pip live on the data volume. A JDK, Rust, PHP, Ruby, and Docker are not installed.

Every start checks the data volume for `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, and `grok`. Anything missing is downloaded there, so the next image rebuild does not fetch them again.

API keys are not downloaded. Give them to yawble (`yawble secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`; `yawble github` for `GH_TOKEN`) and run `yawble up`. yawble keeps them in its own env file, readable only by you, and hands it to the container; nothing is copied into the image. Logins those CLIs save for themselves also persist, because `HOME` is `/data/agent-home` on the same volume.

**Backups.** The host writes a daily `VACUUM INTO` copy of the database to `/data/backups` and keeps the newest seven. That copy lives on the same volume, so also export the whole volume from time to time with `podman volume export`. Both, and how to restore them, are in [docs/ops/backups-logs-and-versions.md](docs/ops/backups-logs-and-versions.md).

**Watching a folder.** A folder-change trigger watches the team's documents with no setup. To watch a network share, mount it on the Windows host, pass it in with another `podman run -v`, and list it under `FileBrowser:Roots` with `"allowWatch": true`. The steps, fields and limits are in [docs/ops/folder-change-triggers.md](docs/ops/folder-change-triggers.md).

`GET /api/agents/auth` reports, per preset, whether the command is on `PATH` and whether it looks authenticated. The board shows a banner when a command is installed but the probe says it is not.

**Updating and releasing.** `scripts\update.ps1` pulls `main`, waits until no agent is running in the container, rebuilds with `dev-up.ps1` and prints the version now running. `scripts\release.ps1` runs both suites, tags `v<yyyy.mm.dd.N>`, publishes the GitHub Release and pushes the image to ghcr.io; `-DryRun` stops before publishing. Both are described in [docs/ops/releases-and-updates.md](docs/ops/releases-and-updates.md).
